speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the characteristics of your generalized nonpruritic rash, specifically regarding its onset, distribution, and whether it blanches under pressure. speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola). The classic presentation of a high fever, followed by a generalized nonpruritic rash starting on the trunk and spreading to extremities, combined with a history of a seizure likely due to febrile convulsions, is highly suggestive of measles. While vaccination is up to date, breakthrough cases occur, and the timeline fits perfectly.
